Bangladesh.banner: Guru Nanak Dev Ji and Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji both visited Bengal, and Bangladesh’s small number of Gurdwaras remember their journeys.

list.a: University of Dhaka campus, near Shahbag
list.p: Gurdwara Nanak Shahi stands on the campus of the University of Dhaka and is the largest and best known of Bangladesh’s handful of Gurdwaras. It honours Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s visit to Dhaka in the early 1500s and is said to have been built around 1830. The domed shrine was restored in 1988–89, when a parkarma verandah was added on all four sides. The sangat gathers on Friday afternoons, when visitors are welcome to join the prayers, and a Sikh research centre stands beside it. Buses to Shahbag and Dhaka University stop close by.

Gurdwara Sangat Tola, in the narrow lanes of old Dhaka near Banglabazar, is linked to Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, who stayed in Dhaka with the local sangat during his travels in Bengal in the 1660s. It is one of the oldest Sikh sites in Bangladesh, and a small Gurdwara still stands here.

Pakistan.banner: Pakistan is home to many of the holiest places in Sikhi, from Nankana Sahib, where Guru Nanak Dev Ji was born, to Kartarpur, where he spent his last years.

provinces.name: Punjab

list.p: Gurdwara Baba Bhuman Shah, near Dipalpur in Okara district, honours Baba Bhuman Shah, an 18th-century Udasi saint known for his langar and devotion to Guru Nanak Dev Ji.

Gurdwara Rori Sahib at Eminabad, near Gujranwala, marks a place where Guru Nanak Dev Ji stayed, sitting on a bed of pebbles (rori) during his travels. Nearby is the home of Bhai Lalo, the humble carpenter who was the Guru’s host.

Gurdwara Panja Sahib at Hasan Abdal holds the rock that, in Sikh tradition, bears the imprint of Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s hand, where he stopped a boulder rolled down the hill by Wali Qandhari. A spring flows from beneath the rock into the sarovar. Built in the time of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, it is one of the most visited Sikh shrines in Pakistan, especially at Vaisakhi.

Gurdwara Darbar Sahib at Kartarpur, on the Ravi river, stands where Guru Nanak Dev Ji spent the last eighteen years of his life, farming the land and teaching, and where he passed away in 1539. Since 2019 the Kartarpur Corridor has let pilgrims from India visit without a visa, crossing the border just a few kilometres away.

Gurdwara Dera Sahib in Lahore, beside the Badshahi Mosque and the Lahore Fort, marks the place of the martyrdom of Guru Arjan Dev Ji in 1606. Next to it stands the samadhi of Maharaja Ranjit Singh. Pilgrims gather here every year for the Guru’s martyrdom day.

list.n: Gurdwara Janam Asthan Guru Ram Das
list.p: Gurdwara Janam Asthan Guru Ram Das, in the Chuna Mandi bazaar of old Lahore, marks the birthplace of Guru Ram Das Ji, the fourth Guru, in 1534. It is one of the historic Sikh shrines of the walled city.

Gurdwara Chhevin Patshahi in Lahore is linked to Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji, the sixth Guru, who came to Lahore to see where his father, Guru Arjan Dev Ji, had been martyred. It is one of the old Sikh shrines of the city.

Gurdwara Shaheed Ganj, near Landa Bazaar in Lahore, honours the Sikhs who were martyred here in the 18th century, including Bhai Mani Singh Ji and Bhai Taru Singh Ji. It is one of the historic Sikh shrines of Lahore.

Gurudwara Baba Baloo Hasna is a historic Sikh shrine in Manhala, Punjab, Pakistan. Many of Pakistan’s Gurdwaras are looked after by the Evacuee Trust Property Board, and some open only for festivals and visiting jathas, so check before you travel.

Gurdwara Janam Asthan in Nankana Sahib marks the place where Guru Nanak Dev Ji was born in 1469, in the village then called Rai Bhoi di Talwandi. It is one of the holiest places in Sikhi, and every year thousands of pilgrims from India and around the world come here for Guru Nanak’s Gurpurab. The present building dates from the time of Maharaja Ranjit Singh.

Gurudwara Sandhawalia is a historic Sikh shrine in Narwar, Punjab, Pakistan. Many of Pakistan’s Gurdwaras are looked after by the Evacuee Trust Property Board, and some open only for festivals and visiting jathas, so check before you travel.

Gurdwara Chowa Sahib, inside the great Rohtas Fort near Jhelum, marks the spring that, in Sikh tradition, appeared when Guru Nanak Dev Ji touched the ground here during his travels. The Gurdwara was built in the time of Maharaja Ranjit Singh.
Gurdwara Beri Sahib in Sialkot stands beside the ber tree under which, in Sikh tradition, Guru Nanak Dev Ji rested when he visited the city. It is one of the historic Sikh shrines of northern Punjab.
